name: wishlist-web
// name: Prefixed, while this workspace's other Next.js app is plainly `web`. Nx project names are global, so `web` was taken; the asymmetry is temporary and `doc/decision/0310-*` records it. Nothing selects applications by name anyway — scripts use the `app:` tag.
// targets: build, dev, start and lint are inferred (@nx/next/plugin, @nx/eslint/plugin). Only the two that need an option are spelled out.

build.// env: Nx injects the workspace-root and project-root `.env` files into every target's environment. Both carry NODE_ENV=development (they are dev env files — see doc/decision/0009-*), which would otherwise leak into `next build` and produce a mixed development/production React resolution. Measured here: without this pin, `next build` warns "You are using a non-standard NODE_ENV value". Same fix as `apps/garage/web`; see doc/decision/0028-*.

start.// env: The same `.env` injection reaches `next start`, which would otherwise serve a production build under NODE_ENV=development — the mixed resolution doc/decision/0028-* is about.

dev.// port: 4300, and it has to be stated. Nx injects the workspace-root `.env` into every target and that file carries PORT=3000 (the let's park API's); `next dev` reads PORT when no `--port` is given, so an unpinned dev target here would bind 3000 and collide. `apps/garage/web` is pinned to 4200 for the same reason — see its project.json and doc/decision/0009-*.
